paragraphs: MenuLogic K12 sells software that its homepage calls a decision support system for school nutrition teams. The product is presented around clarity for the menu, operations, and budget, and confidence for the team. The homepage says technology streamlines operations, enhances efficiency, and provides data-driven insights for better decision-making and resource utilization.

Customers named on the homepage are public school districts and school corporations. That list includes Aurora Public Schools, Perry Township Schools, and Montague Township School District. A school nutrition director quoted on the homepage says the program gives specific profit/loss information on every menu item.

A second page says the software was created by a school nutrition director who had more questions than answers from the data she had to work with. Lindsey Hill, RD, SNS is listed there as Founder and Chief Product Officer. The company says it does not answer to big tech or investors.

quote.text: School nutrition teams choose MenuLogic because it reduces unnecessary complexity, increases accuracy, and delivers the menu-based insight they’ve been missing to manage both operations and budget with confidence.
